# `silk/text/regex`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

ECMAScript Unicode regular expressions for text and JSON Schema patterns.

## When to use
Use `Regex.compile` and `Regex.test` to reuse a `Pattern` across many searches. Use
`Regex.validate` to check syntax or `Regex.matches` for a one-off unanchored search. Patterns
use the ECMA-262 Unicode (`u`) grammar, not shell glob syntax.

## Details
The engine is the QuickJS regular-expression compiler and backtracking matcher as SilkJS ports
it to Silk (QuickJS is Copyright (c) 2017-2021 Fabrice Bellard and Charlie Gordon, under the MIT
license in `licenses/quickjs.txt`). A pattern compiles to bytecode once; a search then runs it
with search hints (literal runs, anchors and first-character sets) and a heap backtracking
stack, so long text never exhausts the native stack. Matching supports captures, named and
numeric backreferences, forward and backward assertions, alternation, character classes, Unicode
properties, greedy and lazy repetition, and scoped `i`, `m`, and `s` modifiers. Unicode
properties and case folding use Unicode 17.0.0.

Text is UTF-8. ASCII text is matched in place; other text is converted to UTF-16 for the
search, and a surrogate pair is one character, as in ECMAScript's `u` mode. Syntax failures
and exhausted resource limits are errors, never a negative match.

Import as `Regex` with `import silk.text.regex { Regex }`.

<a id="Pattern"></a>

## `Pattern`

```silk
pub struct Pattern
```

An owned, immutable ECMAScript Unicode regular-expression program.

### Details
Construct it with `Regex.compile` and search any number of strings with `Regex.test`. It owns
its bytecode and does not borrow the source pattern. Matching does not mutate it.

<a id="Regex.impl.compile"></a>

### Associated function `compile`

```silk
pub effect fn compile(pattern: string) -> Pattern
    ! RegexError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Compiles an ECMAScript Unicode (`u`) pattern for repeated unanchored searches.

#### Details
Patterns have no surrounding slashes or flags. Scoped `(?ims-ims:...)` modifiers are
supported. Captures, backreferences, lookarounds and Unicode property escapes compile to
bytecode; property aliases and case folding use Unicode 17.0.0. The result owns its program
and does not borrow `pattern`.

#### Errors
- `RegexError` with `Syntax` for invalid syntax, or `PatternLimit` for more than 65,536
  pattern bytes, groups nested deeper than 255 levels, 255 or more captures, or too many
  class ranges or nested quantifiers.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the program.

<a id="Regex.impl.validate"></a>

### Associated function `validate`

```silk
pub effect fn validate(pattern: string) -> ()
    ! RegexError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Checks the entire pattern against the ECMAScript Unicode (`u`) grammar.

#### Details
There are no surrounding slashes or flags. Scoped `(?ims-ims:...)` modifiers are accepted.
Unicode property names and values are exact, case-sensitive Unicode 17.0.0 aliases. Legacy
octal and identity escapes are not accepted in Unicode mode.

#### Errors
- `RegexError` with `Syntax` for invalid syntax, or `PatternLimit` for more than 65,536
  pattern bytes, groups nested deeper than 255 levels, 255 or more captures, or too many
  class ranges or nested quantifiers.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the program.

<a id="Regex.impl.matches"></a>

### Associated function `matches`

```silk
pub effect fn matches(pattern: string, text: string) -> bool
    ! RegexError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns whether any substring of `text` matches an ECMAScript Unicode (`u`) pattern.

#### Details
The pattern has no surrounding slashes or flags. Matching is case-sensitive, with `.` excluding
LF, CR, U+2028 and U+2029, unless scoped `i`, `m` or `s` modifiers change those rules. Without
`m`, `^` and `$` mean the actual beginning and end, including when text ends in a newline.
`\d` and `\w` are ASCII classes; `\s` is ECMAScript whitespace and line terminators.
Captures, backreferences and repetition have ECMAScript backtracking order.

#### Errors
- `RegexError` for an invalid pattern, as `Regex.compile` reports it, or `MatchLimit` when
  the search exhausts its work budget. Exhaustion is never reported as `false`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply the program or matcher state.

<a id="Regex.impl.test"></a>

### Associated function `test`

```silk
pub effect fn test(pattern: &Pattern, text: string) -> bool
    ! RegexError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Searches `text` with a previously compiled ECMAScript Unicode pattern.

#### Details
Searches are unanchored unless the pattern supplies anchors. Captures and repetition use
ECMAScript backtracking order. ASCII text is searched in place; other text is first converted
to UTF-16 in storage that belongs to this call. The pattern is immutable.

#### Errors
- `RegexError` with `MatchLimit` after about 1,000,000 backtracking steps. Exhaustion is
  never reported as `false`.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the allocator cannot supply converted text or backtracking storage.
